title: Preoperative classification of histopathological growth patterns in colorectal liver metastases using prospective 18 F-FDG PET/CT

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Preoperative classification of histopathological growth patterns in colorectal liver metastases using prospective 18 F-FDG PET/CT》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · Par7】The overarching aim of this prospective exploratory study was to investigate if FDG-PET/CT can be used in the preoperative setting to non-invasively identify the two most common HGP in CLM patients. Our primary aim was to identify FDG-PET/CT imaging features distinguishing eHGP from rHGP in chemonaïve and pretreated cohorts. Our secondary aim was to investigate if PET parameters (SUVmax, SUVmean or MTV) correlate with overall survival following liver surgery.

【Introduction · Par2】Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the most common malignancies worldwide, and approximately one-third of patients are diagnosed with colorectal liver metastases (CLM) [1]. Liver surgery is paramount in achieving possibility of lasting cure for CLM patients and the 5-year overall survival exceeds 50% for resected CLM patients [2]. At the metastasis-liver interface, CLM display histopathological growth patterns (HGP) that are clinically relevant [3]. The encapsulating (eHGP) and replacement (rHGP) pattern demonstrate both prognostic [3, 4] and potential predictive value [5]. Furthermore, it has been shown that the rHGP is associated with a higher number of R1 resections [6]. Currently, HGP classification relies on histopathological assessment of resected surgical specimens. The lack of feasible preoperative classification consequently limits the clinical integration of HGP into personalised treatment planning.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Preoperative classification of histopathological growth patterns in colorectal liver metastases using prospective 18 F-FDG PET/CT》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study design and patient cohort · Par8】Umeå university hospital is a tertiary hepato-pancreatico-biliary centre serving the four northern regions of Sweden. For this study, patients with CLM were prospectively enrolled from the multidisciplinary team conference (MDT) of CLM if deemed eligible between 1st June 2013 to 31st December 2017. Standard staging included contrast-enhanced liver MRI and CT of the thorax and abdomen; all patients additionally underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT according to national guidelines. Patients with CLM were included in the study when deemed resectable at MDT. Excluded patients were: (1) patients planned for ablative intervention only, (2) patients who did not give their consent, (3) patients who were not able to conceive written or oral information, and (4) patients evaluated with FDG-PET/CT who later did not undergo liver resection for any reason. Patients who did not undergo liver surgery were excluded from further analysis since no tissue sections could be retrieved for HGP classification.

【Study design and patient cohort · Par9】Throughout the study period, the national guidelines recommended FDG-PET/CT for staging of all patients with metastatic CRC. Clinical data were collected from medical charts. The date of deaths was obtained from the Swedish population register. Prior to analysing the FDG-PET/CT results, we divided the patient cohort into chemonaïve and pretreated groups, since pre-imaging chemotherapy significantly alters metabolic activity, necessitating subgroup analysis [22].

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Preoperative classification of histopathological growth patterns in colorectal liver metastases using prospective 18 F-FDG PET/CT》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Metabolic PET activity matches histopathological findings in 130 classifiable CLM · Par33】A total of 135 CLM (69 patients) showed FDG-avid lesions concordant with MRI segment localisation and had available tissue sections; 5 CLM were non-classifiable due to absence of viable tumour on tissue sections, leaving 130 classifiable CLM for PET–HGP analyses. Figure 3 illustrates patient and CLM selection based on PET metabolic activity linked to tissue sections from the same liver segment. Details regarding CLM without PET uptake or not identified on MRI are provided in Supplementary Information 1.

【Conclusion · Par51】No reliable associations were identified between FDG-PET parameters and HGP. The evaluated PET parameters therefore appear to have limited value for non-invasive HGP prediction, warranting further investigation and exploration of alternative non-invasive biomarkers including other imaging biomarkers.

【Statistical analysis · Par21】Statistical analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics version 25.0 (Mac OS X, Armonk, New York, USA: IBM Corp.) and R version 4.1.1 [23]. Continuous variables were analysed for normal distribution, and differences were calculated using the Mann-Whitney U test. Categorical variables were analysed using the chi-square test of association or Fisher’s exact test when applicable.
